summary: Tavivat Puntarigvivat works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned an M.A. from the University of Hawaiʻi and studied under Luangpor Teean Jittasubho in 1980. His career includes posts at Mahidol University, World Buddhist University, and Kyoto University.

Taw Sein Ko (1864–1930) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Rangoon, the Inner Temple (circa 1892–1893), and the Inns of Court (circa 1892–1893).

Teizo Iyanaga (1915–1983) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (c. 1935–1938), he held posts at Nagoya University (c. 1949–1960), the University of Tokyo (c. 1960–1976), and Sophia University (c. 1976–1983).

Tej Ram Sharma (born 1941) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral thesis at Banaras Hindu University in 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University around 1972.
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Lobsang Gyatso. He also taught Lobsang Gyatso.

Tenga Rinpoche (1932–2012) was an expert in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Benchen Monastery. He founded Benchen Monastery in 1976 and served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery from around 1967 to 1980.

Tensei Kitabatake (1928–2024) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (c. 1950–1955). He served at Ryukoku as professor, dean, and president (1995–1999), and later as president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye (1938–2003) specialized in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sogen Omori, whom he succeeded, and founded Daihonzan Chozen-ji.
Tenzin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Philosophy degree at the University of Oslo, where he studied under supervisor Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).

Tenzin Dhargye (b. 1968) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Sera Monastery and Gyume Tantric College under Ling Rinpoche, he taught at both institutions, was a guest lecturer at the University of Virginia, and directed Tibetzentrum Österreich.

Tenzin Dorjee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Geshe Dawa, and served as General Secretary at Pullahari Monastery and translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.
Tenzin L. Mullin is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. Mullin earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Otago, studying under the supervision of Elizabeth Guthrie.

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche (b. 1961) works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Geshe degree at Menri Monastery and served as director of the Dialectic School of Menri before founding Ligmincha International in 1992.

Ter Ellingson (born 1944) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin–Madison, and served as a professor of music at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

Terese Tse Bartholomew is a specialist in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology who earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles. She served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum.

Terrell Carver (born 1946) specializes in philosophy. He studied at Columbia University (c. 1964–1968) and the University of Oxford (c. 1970–1974), and held posts at the University of Liverpool (c. 1974–1979) and the University of Bristol (c. 1980).

Terry Kleeman (b. 1955) is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (c. 1983–1988) and became a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder around 1998.

Terton Sogyal (1856–1926) was a scholar and master in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Pema Vajra 01, and Patrul Rinpoche, and his students included the 13th Dalai Lama.

Teruji Ishizu (1903–1972) studied at the University of Tokyo. Active in religious studies and philosophy, he held posts at Nihon University and the University of Tokyo, served as president of Tohoku University and Miyagi University of Education, and taught at Keio and Komazawa.

Tessa Bartholomeusz (1958–2001) specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Florida, Florida State, and Virginia (PhD 1991), and held posts at Virginia, Florida State (1993), and Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis (c. 1991–2001).
